newsitem.title: UK: Dlr firmer in Europe as U.S. asset markets recover.
newsitem.headline: Dlr firmer in Europe as U.S. asset markets recover.

text.p: The dollar recovered during a quiet European session as firmer U.S. asset markets prompted short-covering after Thursday's fall.

Dealers and analysts said the dollar's fortunes in the near term will continue to depend on the performance on the U.S. stock and bond markets. Any more strong data will only raise speculation of a credit tightening and if that hurts asset markets the dollar will fall.
At 1530 GMT the dollar was at 1.5563/68 marks and 116.13/23 yen, up from an opening 1.5449/56 and 115.54/64 and Thursday's 1.5406/26 and 115.45/50.
Wall Street managed to claw back 50 points of Thursday's heavy losses and Treasuries were steady after their sharp falls.

"It seemed a good bet that the U.S. (asset markets) would open higher today and a lot of European players were bidding hard for dollars this morning," said one trader at a leading U.S. bank. "Everyone seemed to ignore the construction spending even though it was much stronger than expected but I think that's because everyone is just fixated with Wall Street."
The dollar gained in late business despite a much stronger than expected 1.9 percent rise in U.S. November construction spending.
Construction spending rose 1.9 percent in November after a 1.5 percent increase in October, way above market forecasts for a 0.6 percent decline.
Analysts said in the near term the dollar should continue to do well, providing the asset markets hold up, but further out things do not look so rosy.
"People are still in the mood to buy dollars and there is little on the immediate horizon to change that mindset," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.
He said that next Friday's U.S. payrolls data could well be a watershed if the number turns out stronger than expected.
Also, trade with Japan lingers in the background and if dollar/yen continues to firm it is only a matter of time before it begins to grate with U.S. officials, analysts said.

The mark was generally slightly higher on the European crosses at 3.3792/96 French francs from 3.3758/62 earlier but it was down slightly on the Swiss franc after recent strength at 86.97/99 centimes from 87.11/13 earlier.

Sterling rebounded after Thursday's losses but cable was prone to profit-taking and was unable to hold above $1.70. It was at $1.6920/30 in late business against a $1.7015 high and Thursday's close of $1.6885/95.
